descriptionChirho: The proper name Koresh (כּוֹרֶשׁ), referring to Cyrus II ('the Great'), king of Persia (r. 559-530 BCE), who conquered Babylon and issued the decree permitting the Jewish exiles to return and rebuild the Temple. All 15 occurrences refer to this single historical figure, appearing in 2 Chronicles 36:22-23, Ezra 1:1-8, 3:7, 4:3,5, 5:13-17, 6:3,14, Isaiah 44:28, 45:1, and Daniel 1:21, 6:28, 10:1. English renders as Cyrus/Koresh; Spanish Ciro/Koresh; Hindi कोरेश (Koresh); Arabic كُورَشُ (Kurash); Korean 고레스 (Goreseu); Swahili Koreshi. Both clusters denote the same king — transliteration differences (Koresh vs. Cyrus) are merely rendering conventions, not distinct referents.
